title: User-journey SLI mapping and query-cost notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a concrete, pragmatic approach to tie observable signals (metrics + traces) to high-level user journeys for inference workloads, and to measure per-query token-cost attribution so we can build cost-aware dashboards and alerts. It's intentionally opinionated: I want something implementable in the next quarter rather than an exhaustive taxonomy.

Scope / goals:
- Define a minimal SLI set per user-journey (chat, batch-embed, rerank, long-context completion) that directly maps to user-visible quality and latency.
- Establish tracing anchors / span boundaries to attribute latency and failures to components (router, kv-cache, serving runtime, fallback model).
- Propose dashboard panels and drilldowns that combine SLI health + token-cost per-journey + top contributors.
- Sketch sampling rules and retention needed for post-incident cost/quality analysis.

High-level user journeys (for SLI purposes):
1) Chat (interactive, streaming): short-turn latency and return-of-first-byte, progressive token stream health, abrupt cutoffs.
2) Assistant long-form (long-context, single response): end-to-end completion latency and generation quality (regression checks).
3) Embeddings batch: throughput, per-item latency, and tokenization anomalies.
4) Rerank / pairwise: request/response latency and success-rate (models finishing scoring vs timed-out).

Minimal SLI set (per journey) — rationale and concrete metrics:
- Availability (binary): percentage of requests that returned a successful 2xx non-empty response within a configured deadline (chat: 3s to first token, completion: 15s total). Metric: count(request_success and latency < deadline) / count(requests).
- P50/P95 latency: for interactive journeys track first-token latency and 95th for tail behavior. Metric: histogram(bucketed by token-phase).
- Token-cost per request (est.): total model tokens consumed * per-token cost profile. Metric: sum(token_count * token_price_profile) grouped by journey.
- Quality regression signal (synthetic prompts): percent of eval prompts that produce a score delta > threshold. Metric: synthetic_eval_fail_rate.
- KV-cache hit rate: cache_hits / cache_lookups per journey. Important for cost and latency.
- Fallback rate: percent of requests routed to lower-tier model due to capacity/errors.

Trace and span model (recommendation):
- Root span: request-received (attributes: journey, customer_id, route, pinned_model, request_size_tokens).
- Router span: policy-eval (attributes: route_policy, capacity_hint, selected_model_version).
- Cache span (KV-cache): lookup span(s), with attributes cache_key, hit=true|false, evicted=true|false, ttl_remaining. If hit, include cached_response_size_tokens.
- Serving runtime span: compile/prepare (if cold), execute/generate (per-token sub-spans optional aggregated), kv-invalidate if eviction during generate. Attributes: model_variant, quantization, gpu_type, batch_id, batch_size_at_submit.
- Network/transport span (if relevant): streaming connection open / first-byte / last-byte.
- Post-processing span: token-filtering, function-call formatting.
- Fallback span: invoked if primary model errored or exceeded latency SLO. Attribute fallback_reason.

Sampling and retention strategy (pragmatic):
- High sampling for errors and fallback flows: sample 100% of traces where status != 200 or fallback_rate true.
- 5% sampling for successful interactive chat requests by default; 15% for high-cost (> 10k tokens) requests.
- Synthetic probes: 1/minute per region for each major journey to baseline latency and token-cost drift. Store full traces for synthetic probes for 90 days.
- Keep aggregated metrics (histograms, counts) at full resolution for 365 days; keep sampled traces (the trace payloads) for 30 days.

Token-cost attribution approach (approximate but actionable):
- Instrument per-request token_counts: prompt_tokens, generated_tokens, cached_tokens_returned. Multiply by model-tier price-table (hosted price or internal cost estimate).
- Chargebacks: aggregate at route/customer_id/model_variant weekly. Dashboard shows per-journey median and 95th cost per request.
- For cases with mixed model pipeline (rerank after embedding): attribute cost to pipeline_step in proportions (e.g., embedding: 30%, rerank: 70%) — keep exact breakdown columns.

Dashboard suggestions (layout and panels):
Top-level "Journey Health" (single view):
- Row per journey: Availability %, P95 latency, median token-cost, KV-hit rate, fallback %. Color-coded heatmap for quick triage.
- Click a journey row -> opens journey detail page.

Journey detail page (chat example):
- Timeline: synthetic probe latency + first-token p95 overlay.
- Histogram: first-token latency distribution (buckets: <50ms, 50-150ms, 150-500ms, 500-1500ms, >1500ms).
- Cost panel: distribution of per-request token-cost, top 10 customers by spend in time window.
- Trace-sampled waterfall: top slow traces aggregated by span contribution (router/cache/runtime/transport).
- KV-cache health: hit rate, eviction rate, percent of requests with cache_hot_path (true).
- Alerts summary: active SLO burn rate alerts and recent incidents.

Drilldown queries (examples to implement):
- SELECT journey, histogram(bucketed_first_token_latency) FROM requests WHERE status=200 AND time > now()-1h GROUP BY journey
- Top contributors to cost: group by customer_id, sum(token_cost) ORDER BY sum DESC LIMIT 20
- Cache eviction debugger: traces where cache_hit=false AND serving_runtime_latency > p95 AND kv_evicted=true

Alerting proposals (practical thresholds to iterate):
- Journey availability < 99.5% over 15m => P1 follow SRE runbook.
- First-token p95 (chat) > 1200ms over 15m and synthetic probes also degraded => investigate routing/backpressure.
- KV-cache hit rate drop > 8 percentage points vs baseline (24h rolling) => auto paging to caching-team.
- Cost spike: weekly token-cost for a customer grows > 3x vs trailing 4-week median => notify CS and billing.

Implementation TODOs (owners + rough ETA):
- Add per-request token_count fields to request metrics (prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, cached_tokens) — owner: Ravi — ETA: 2w.
- Expand trace spans to include cache attributes and eviction flags — owner: Samira — ETA: 3w.
- Dashboard templates (Journey Health + Chat Detail) — owner: Maya — ETA: 4w.
- Synthetic probe definitions + scheduled runner + retention policy — owner: SRE/infra (Evan) — ETA: 6w.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How precise does cost attribution need to be for internal billing? We can start with approximate token-based chargebacks but customers may demand per-microsecond GPU-seconds later.
- Sampling: is our storage budget for traces sufficient to hold full traces for 30 days? If not, reduce baseline sampling and keep synthetic traces.
- Should we capture per-token timing (sub-span per token) for fine-grained latency attribution? That gives great signal but multiplies trace volume and complexity. For now prefer aggregated serving_runtime spans with optional sampled per-token traces for top 1% long requests.

Quick checklist for next 2 sprints:
- [ ] Merge token_count metric PR (ENG-2314)
- [ ] Add cache eviction flag to traces
- [ ] Build Journey Health dashboard skeleton (share JSON dashboard in repo)
- [ ] Start synthetic probe runner in two regions

Notes to reviewers:
- Focus review on the SLI definitions and alert thresholds — these are policy-level decisions and will affect incident paging.
- If you have specific customer chargeback requirements, add a comment under JIRA-ENG-2314 — we should capture those as constraints before we finalize cost dashboards.

References and inspirations:
- Internal: OBS-journeys confluence (linked).
- External: "Monitoring distributed systems: user journeys and SLIs" (operational best-practice paper) — recommended for the team if we want deeper material.

Version history:
- 2025-01-15 initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-01-28 added token-cost attribution and sampling notes (Ravi)
- 2025-02-12 updated dashboard layout and owner TODOs (Samira)

End.
